development_policy.replacement_rule: A confirmed rule supersedes, but never rewrites, the prior decision. Recompile the package, dataset and golden controls with new checksums.
development_policy.answer_disclosure_rule: Every answer must disclose the constructed-synthetic dataset and cite all provisional decision IDs that materially affect the result.

decisions.statement: Treat all supplied sample rows, metric results and inferred controls as constructed synthetic and not customer-validated.
decisions.rationale: The External Reviewer email explicitly labels the sample as generated/synthetic and explains that customer materials cannot be exported.
decisions.risk_and_limitations: The PoC proves product behavior against an internally controlled case, not correctness against customer production data.

decisions.statement: Normalize the British spelling CANCELLED to the source enum CANCELED.
decisions.rationale: The data dictionary and sample consistently use CANCELED; one metric transcription uses CANCELLED.
decisions.risk_and_limitations: No semantic change is intended; production adapters may preserve a different physical spelling.

decisions.statement: Use venue_code + trading_date + order_id as the observed order-lifecycle key.
decisions.rationale: The metric transcription names this grain; order_id alone may be reused across venues or dates.
decisions.risk_and_limitations: The synthetic window contains lifecycles whose NEW event is not observed and some events that appear out of lifecycle order.

decisions.statement: Do not infer that the one-week order sample contains complete lifecycles.
decisions.rationale: Of 1,400 observed order IDs, only 1,000 contain a NEW event; all 400 order IDs referenced by the 200 trades have no NEW event. Some CANCEL or MODIFY events sort before NEW using the supplied ordering fields.
decisions.risk_and_limitations: Lifecycle KPIs are provisional; the self-trade timeline reports observed records without claiming completeness.

decisions.statement: A potential self-trade candidate is an eligible active trade whose normalized buy and sell participant IDs are both present and equal.
decisions.chosen_rule: activity_type=TRADE AND trade_status=ACTIVE AND buy_participant_id IS NOT NULL AND sell_participant_id IS NOT NULL AND normalize(buy_participant_id)=normalize(sell_participant_id)
decisions.rationale: This is the only explicit candidate rule in the supplied metric logic and analytical question.
decisions.risk_and_limitations: The equality is a triage signal only and is not evidence of market abuse, intent or regulatory breach.

decisions.statement: Use all eligible active trades with both-side participant IDs as the self-trade-rate denominator.
decisions.rationale: This matches the written formula and avoids silently treating unavailable participant IDs as non-self-trades.
decisions.risk_and_limitations: Production data may require a clearing-participant, account, beneficial-owner or group-level identity instead.

decisions.statement: Exclude canceled, busted and corrected-original trade records from eligible-trade metrics.
decisions.chosen_rule: include ACTIVE TRADE rows; exclude CANCEL/BUST/CORRECT events and any original row referenced by an included correction
decisions.rationale: The active-volume transcription requests this behavior, while the synthetic sample contains only ACTIVE TRADE rows and no references.
decisions.risk_and_limitations: Reference direction and valid correction states require production confirmation.

decisions.statement: Trade capture latency is receive_timestamp minus transaction_timestamp in integer milliseconds for eligible active trades.
decisions.chosen_rule: latency_ms=round((receive_timestamp-transaction_timestamp)*1000); negative values excluded and counted as exceptions; percentiles use nearest-rank
decisions.rationale: The supplied definition specifies the timestamps and exception behavior but not the percentile algorithm.
decisions.risk_and_limitations: No SLA or threshold-breach classification is produced until a threshold is supplied or deliberately simulated.

decisions.statement: For the synthetic demo, a client participant is an account_reference row with participant_type=CLIENT effective for the trade.
decisions.rationale: The dictionary supplies this controlled value but no entitlement/client hierarchy rule.
decisions.risk_and_limitations: Production identity may be account-, participant-, member-, client-group- or beneficial-owner-based.

decisions.statement: Label trade_notional as HKD and base_notional_before_haircut as USD for the supplied sample.
decisions.rationale: The sample multiplies HKD notional by HKD-to-USD exchange rates; the metric text incorrectly asks for HKD after conversion.
decisions.risk_and_limitations: The PoC will show both native HKD notional and converted USD notional and will not relabel one as the other.

decisions.statement: Define a submitted-order attempt as a distinct observed lifecycle containing a NEW or REJECT event.
decisions.chosen_rule: submitted_order_attempt=distinct lifecycle with any activity_type in [NEW,REJECT]
decisions.rationale: Rejected submissions may not have a NEW event; counting every mid-window lifecycle as submitted would misstate the denominator.
decisions.risk_and_limitations: This is an internal executable convention for the incomplete one-week sample, not an customer definition.

decisions.statement: Count a rejected submitted order when any eligible event in its observed lifecycle has activity_type=REJECT or order_status=REJECTED.
decisions.chosen_rule: rejected_submitted_order=eligible submitted order with any REJECT/REJECTED event
decisions.rationale: The business definition says terminal or event outcome includes a rejection; a rejection-only lifecycle has no later terminal state.
decisions.risk_and_limitations: Production cancellation/rejection correction rules remain to be confirmed.

decisions.statement: For cancel-to-trade, count distinct observed order lifecycles containing a CANCEL event and divide by distinct eligible active trades for the same cohort.
decisions.chosen_rule: cancel_to_trade_ratio=distinct lifecycle with activity_type=CANCEL/distinct eligible active trade_id
decisions.rationale: The supplied row mixes cancel events and final CANCELED status; this rule preserves the metric name's event interpretation.
decisions.risk_and_limitations: A separate terminal-canceled-order metric will be exposed so the two meanings cannot be confused.

decisions.statement: For order-to-trade, divide distinct submitted-order attempts by two times distinct eligible active trades.
decisions.rationale: This preserves the explicitly supplied two-sided matching convention.
decisions.risk_and_limitations: The multiplier may not apply to aggregated, auction, internalized or multi-leg executions in production.

decisions.statement: Produce one workbook with one worksheet per participant plus CSV export files, rather than a sheet named .csv.
decisions.chosen_rule: interactive_workbook=one participant per sheet; machine_export=one participant CSV per file
decisions.rationale: The requested wording combines an Excel sheet with a CSV filename, which are different output containers.
decisions.risk_and_limitations: Participant sheet names will be sanitized to Excel limits while the original participant ID remains in a visible cell.

decisions.statement: Apply a demo-only policy: surveillance and trading demo roles may inspect synthetic row-level identifiers; markets demo role receives aggregate measures and redacted participant identifiers; surveillance is limited to 3 months.
decisions.rationale: The requirements give role-level intentions but not a complete entitlement model.
decisions.risk_and_limitations: This does not represent production IAM, database row-level security or customer policy approval.

decisions.statement: Generate known-correct controls independently from typed derived data; do not label compiler-generated SQL or derived answers as External Reviewer/customer-provided controls.
decisions.rationale: No existing SQL or independently approved expected results were supplied.
decisions.risk_and_limitations: The control proves internal consistency of the synthetic case, not customer business correctness.

decisions.statement: Use calendar_code + business_date as the logical calendar key.
decisions.rationale: The overview lists business_date alone but the dictionary notes that multiple calendars require a composite key.
decisions.risk_and_limitations: The supplied sample has only one calendar, so the difference is not observable in current controls.

decisions.statement: Treat the actual worksheet header counts as authoritative for the synthetic packet: 68 order fields and 45 trade fields.
decisions.rationale: The data-model overview says 70 and 47, but each detailed dictionary and sample sheet has 68 and 45 exact matching headers.
decisions.risk_and_limitations: This corrects packet metadata only and says nothing about the eventual production schema.

decisions.statement: Interpret business dates in Asia/Hong_Kong and persist event timestamps as UTC instants after source-timezone assignment.
decisions.rationale: The scenario is HK cash trading, while the dictionary requests UTC normalization but does not state whether spreadsheet timestamps are already UTC.
decisions.risk_and_limitations: Latency differences are timezone-invariant when both timestamps share the same source convention, but displayed wall time may change after confirmation.
